edges.description: Loss of Smoothened blocks transduction of the Hedgehog signal.
Reduced Hedgehog patterning of the ventral diencephalon produces hypothalamic hamartoma.
Altered Hedgehog limb patterning produces postaxial polydactyly.
Defective Hedgehog-dependent cardiac morphogenesis produces atrioventricular septal defect.
Impaired Hedgehog-dependent enteric neural crest development produces aganglionosis.
The hamartoma forms an intrinsically epileptogenic network causing gelastic seizures.

Confirms Smo as the obligatory Hedgehog transducer and reproduces the Hedgehog-loss developmental phenotype, including cardiac morphogenesis defects relevant to the human atrioventricular septal defect.
edges.limitations: The homozygous null is embryonic-lethal with cyclopia/holoprosencephaly, far more severe than the viable human recessive syndrome, so it does not reproduce the hypothalamic hamartoma; it models the Hedgehog-transduction mechanism rather than the human phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Bi-allelic Variations of SMO in Humans Cause a Broad Spectrum of Developmental Anomalies Due to Abnormal Hedgehog Signaling.
evidence.snippet: these variations cause a wide phenotypic spectrum of developmental anomalies affecting the brain (hypothalamic hamartoma and microcephaly), heart (atrioventricular septal defect), skeleton (postaxial polydactyly, narrow chest, and shortening of long bones), and enteric nervous system (aganglionosis).

nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function SMO variants leave absent or non-functional Smoothened, the obligatory transducer of Hedgehog signalling downstream of PTCH1 at the primary cilium.

evidence.reference_title: A familial syndrome of hypothalamic hamartomas, polydactyly, and SMO mutations: a clinical report of 2 cases.
evidence.snippet: Hypothalamic hamartomas are benign tumors known to cause gelastic or dacrystic seizures, precocious puberty, developmental delay, and medically refractory epilepsy.

nodes.description: Patient cells show normal ciliogenesis but severely altered Hedgehog signal transduction, with Hh-independent accumulation of GLI2 at the ciliary tip, indicating that SMO loss disrupts ciliary trafficking and GLI processing. Reduced Hedgehog output during embryogenesis produces the malformation continuum.
